elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Retained 7.2 (and 7.1) still require Teleglobe USA Inc. to bear its Schedule B proportion of O&M Costs; the insertion only caps that commitment to a rolling 12-month period rather than eliminating it.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Payment obligation remains a proportionate share of pooled O&M Costs under Schedule B, not a usage- or order-based charge; the inserted true-up is to "O&M Costs actually incurred", i.e. cost-sharing, not usage pricing.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "commitment to bear O&M Costs under Subparagraph 7.2 is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period, such periods commencing on the RFS Date and each anniversary of it" — a defined, anchored 12-month window that overrides the 25-year lock-in in 18.1 for the recurring O&M spend.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "and may be reduced by Teleglobe USA Inc. on thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — an unconditional Customer-side reduction right at the required notice period.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "On any such reduction or any shortfall against that commitment, Teleglobe USA Inc. shall pay only its proportionate share of O&M Costs actually incurred for the period concerned, trued up to actual cost, and no penalty, forfeiture, reclamation of capacity or acceleration shall apply in respect of the reduced amount." The express disapplication of 23.1 reclamation for the reduced amount removes the forfeiture-style consequence.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted subparagraph delivers all three fallback elements (12-month scope anchored to the RFS Date and anniversaries, 30 days' reduction notice, and a true-up to O&M Costs actually incurred with penalty/forfeiture/reclamation/acceleration expressly disapplied for the reduced amount).
Preferred is correctly not claimed: Schedule B proportionate cost-bearing under 7.1/7.2 survives, so a minimum commitment remains and fees are not usage- or order-based.

Minimality holds: the change is a single concise insertion with no deletions; favourable existing language (Schedule B proportions, 13.2/14.1 upgrade protections, 18.1 term, 23.1 default machinery for amounts actually owed) is retained, and the anti-penalty list is necessary to displace the 23.1 reclamation consequence that would otherwise operate as a shortfall penalty.

Intent preserved: the insertion is expressly framed as a limitation on the Subparagraph 7.2 obligation, so retained 7.2 is not left contradictory; 23.1 continues to apply to amounts genuinely due, the 18.1 duration and one-year exit notice survive, and no term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Residual (not a fallback failure, note in rationale only): the cap reaches O&M Costs only, so the Capital Costs obligation in 7.1 and the "No credit for capital costs" exit consequence remain; this is defensible because Capital Costs are a one-off build contribution settled under 7.7 rather than a recurring purchase commitment, but the comment should say so if the counterparty pushes back.
Drafting nit: the operative insertion carries no subparagraph number although the margin comment calls it "Subparagraph 7.2A" — add the "7.2A" label so the comment and the rendered clause match.
